messages:
Ana Patel: Quick post-all-hands thread — wanted to capture the leadership answers about regional GPU supply and our contingency playbook. Summarizing Qs and adding a couple follow-ups.

Mike Chen: TL;DR from infra: 3 layers — pre-warm pools in target regions, cross-region burst routing, and model-fallback profiles (quantized / smaller families) as last resort. No immediate SLA changes planned.

Tara Singh: Clarify: when you say pre-warm, are we talking dedicated capacity reservations or ephemeral pre-started instances on burstable hosts?

Mike Chen: Good Q. Pre-warm = short-reserved warmers we spin up for ~12-18hr windows around expected demand (based on forecasts). Not full Dedicated reservations — cheaper but not instant.

Dylan R: How do Dedicated customers get prioritized during cross-region bursts? Will we route them cross-region or throttle host-wide?

Mike Chen: Dedicated remains pinned to customer tenancy by default. Cross-region routing only applies to hosted tiers. For Dedicated we have a separate escalation (manual reassignment or temporary bursting to compatible Dedicated pools in another region with customer ok).

Jules (SRE): Action item: create an ops playbook entry for the Dedicated escalation flow — steps, contact list, and expected customer comms. I'll own the doc.

Ana Patel: Leadership also mentioned model-fallbacks — can someone put a short list of recommended fallback profiles (model family + quant) that we should expose in Console rollout options?

Tara Singh: From Product: recommended defaults for fallback: `redwood-xxl-q4-8bit` and `open-llama-13b-q4` for gen, plus `distil-embed-768` for embeddings. We'll surface these with clear perf/cost tradeoffs.

Dylan R: Ops question — what telemetry should we run to detect imminent regional pressure so pre-warms trigger automatically? CPU/GPU utilization alone is noisy. Suggest tracking: queued request growth (>20% over 5m), median tail latency increase, and KV-cache hit drops.

Mike Chen: Agreed. We'll add a composite signal: queued growth + token-emit latency + error rate. Ops team will prototype thresholds this week.

Ana Patel: Can we also get a short blurb for customers about what to expect during a region shortage? E.g., transparent routing + opt-in cross-region, or being pinned with possible increased latency?

Tara Singh: Yep — I'll draft a customer-facing FAQ. Key points: no silent model swaps for Dedicated, hosted customers may be routed cross-region unless they opt out, explicit notice for long (>2hr) disruptions.

Jules (SRE): On-call note: please add a Runbook entry for the new composite pressure signal and the manual pre-warm trigger (snippet below).

Jules (SRE): ```
# manual prewarm trigger
./infractl region prewarm --region=eu-central-1 --pool=burst-warm-6 --duration=12h
```

Ana Patel: Perfect. Who will own the cross-region cost/chargeback model so Billing can update pricing guidance?

Mike Chen: I'll sync with Finance and Billing — expect a proposed chargeback table by EOD Friday.

Tara Singh: Wrap-up: Jules to own ops playbook + runbook snippets, Mike to own billing chargeback draft, Dylan to prototype composite signal, Tara to draft customer FAQ. I'll put these as action items in the all-hands follow-up doc.

Ana Patel: Thanks all — this captures the answers and next steps. If anything else comes up from the recording, drop it here. :white_check_mark:
